items.prompt: Comparison-based sorting lower bound in the algebraic decision-tree model is?
items.whyRight: There are n! permutations; each comparison has two outcomes.
whyWrong: Linear is achievable only with stronger assumptions (counting/radix).
Log n cannot separate n! orders.
Quadratic is an upper bound for slow sorts, not the lower bound.

choices: Equal keys keep their original relative order
The algorithm never uses extra memory

items.prompt: When keys are integers in a small range, a strong option is?
whyWrong: Heap sort is fine but comparison-based.
Binary search finds, does not sort.

choices: Average O(n log n), worst O(n²) on bad pivots
items.whyRight: Balanced pivots give n log n; sorted inputs with naive pivots degrade.
whyWrong: Linear average is false for comparison quicksort.
Worst case is quadratic, not log.

choices: Θ(1) always in the classic top-down form
Θ(log n) data only with no recursion stack
items.whyRight: Merging two runs needs a temporary buffer (plus stack frames).
whyWrong: Stack is log n but data buffer is linear.

items.prompt: Interview: pick a sort — name which axes?
choices: Time bound, stability need, key type/range, memory
items.whyRight: Those constraints decide mergesort vs quicksort vs counting/radix.
whyWrong: Pivot aesthetics are not a criterion.
